notes: Deep learning gene finder (CNN + BiLSTM + HMM). Depends on closed-source precompiled HMM wheels (hidten, bricks2marble); requires GPU with >=8 GB VRAM.
NCBI eukaryotic gene annotation pipeline. Heavy Nextflow orchestrator chaining Gnomon, STAR, miniprot; demands 32 cores, 256 GB RAM; fails on diverse non-model clades.
Ab initio cross-species gene finder using hybrid CNN-BiLSTM. Decoupled from HMMs but lacks explicit grammar graph pathfinder; separate fungal/land plant models.
Pipeline combining GeneMark and AUGUSTUS using RNA-seq (BRAKER1), protein (BRAKER2), or both (BRAKER3). High setup complexity and long multi-stage runtime.
Classic generalized HMM (GHMM) ab initio and evidence-based gene predictor. Fast C++ engine; constrained by geometric/semi-Markov duration limits and single-isoform Viterbi.
Ultra-fast protein-to-genome spliced aligner with custom heuristic dynamic programming. Highly efficient C codebase with zero heavy external dependencies.
Automated eukaryotic gene finder integrating RNA-seq and protein homology into iterative self-training HMM. Strict non-commercial licensing restricts open pipelines.
Automated gene annotation using miniprot spliced protein alignments and AUGUSTUS. Lightweight alternative to BRAKER2 for large genomes.
Semi-HMM ab initio gene prediction engine written in C. Lightweight and adaptable, but struggles with accuracy on complex vertebrate gene architectures.
Comparative gene predictor using dual-genome alignments and machine-learning scoring of splice signals. Early proof-of-concept for alignment-driven feature decoding.
